scope: Six linked College of Science handbook policy pages; requirement-note observations only. No degree completeness or course metadata review.

advising.title: Advising and Registration Policies
advising.locator: main#content, excluding breadcrumbs and navigation/sidebar; all policy text and visible link targets
advising.heading: Advising and Registration Policies

notes.title: Semester advising and registration
notes.summary: College of Science students meet their assigned advisor each semester/term about degree progress, course selection and experiential learning. The advisor prepares an ACRF; the student reviews recommendations and submits the CRF by the pre-registration deadline. Open-registration schedule changes follow advisor consultation; PINs become available in MyPurdue then. These are registration procedures, not additional degree credits.

notes.title: Advising appointment conditions
notes.summary: Regular appointments last 30 minutes; arrival more than five minutes late may lead to cancellation. One registration appointment is allowed per semester/term, with cancellation at least 24 hours ahead. Extenuating circumstances may be considered, but replacement pre-registration appointments depend on availability; failure to cancel may defer service until open registration. Ten-minute drop-ins handle urgent matters, not registration or degree planning, and are first-come without guaranteed availability. The assigned advisor handles students; the page gives a two-business-day email response window and Monday–Friday 8am–5pm EST office hours.

core-overlap.title: Science Core Curriculum Policies
core-overlap.locator: main#content, excluding breadcrumbs and navigation/sidebar; all policy text and visible link targets
core-overlap.heading: Using a Course to Meet Multiple Requirements

notes.title: Science Core multiple-use restriction
notes.summary: A course may satisfy multiple requirements only as allowed by the applicable College and department policies; permissions vary by degree. One course may satisfy only one of Great Issues, Culture/Diversity and General Education. This does not establish permission for any other specific overlap.

credit-raise.title: Credit Raise Policy
credit-raise.locator: main#content, excluding breadcrumbs and navigation/sidebar; all policy text and visible link targets
credit-raise.heading: Credit Raise Policy

notes.title: Credit overload request eligibility
notes.summary: Advisor approval is required to exceed 18 semester hours in fall/spring or nine in summer. A request requires at least a 3.0 cumulative GPA and prior successful completion of the maximum allowable semester load of 18 or summer load of nine, as applicable. These are enrollment limits and request qualifications, not extra degree requirements.

notes.title: Credit overload discretionary review
notes.summary: Approval depends on a holistic review of the proposed course load and the likelihood of passing at grades consistent with prior performance. Approval is not guaranteed and decisions cannot be appealed. The Director of Academic Advising reviews every request exceeding 21 credit hours; the page does not state a separate maximum approved load.

course-repeat.title: Course Repeat Policy
course-repeat.locator: main#content, excluding breadcrumbs and navigation/sidebar; all policy text and visible link targets
course-repeat.heading: Course Repeat Policy

notes.title: Non-repeatable course attempt limit
notes.summary: A non-repeatable course normally permits at most three attempts; a transcript W counts as an attempt. Failure to complete a degree requirement within University rules can prevent continued pursuit of that degree. The required minimum grade remains specific to the degree requirement; this page supplies no replacement GPA rule.

notes.title: Conditional fourth and final attempt
notes.summary: A fourth attempt requires a University-regulation waiver, is not guaranteed and cannot be appealed. The student first discusses extenuating circumstances with the advisor; if those justify review, the advisor supplies the request form. The request explains prior unsuccessful attempts and a plan for success on the fourth and final attempt. The Director of Academic Advising reviews it. Only after an approval decision may the student submit the Scheduling Assistant registration override.

pass-not-pass.title: Pass/Not Pass Policy
pass-not-pass.locator: main#content, excluding breadcrumbs and navigation/sidebar; all policy text and visible link targets
pass-not-pass.heading: Pass/Not Pass Option Policy

notes.title: Pass/not-pass eligibility and unresolved level label
notes.summary: The page permits free electives and, literally, courses at the “5000-level general education requirement” to meet degree requirements. It separately excludes courses required by majors, minors, other departmental requirements, interdisciplinary science core or science core curriculum from elected P/NP grading. Preserve that stated general-education exception and unusual level label; this source alone does not establish that it means 50000-level or authorize other Science Core courses. Students retain the same course obligations as letter-graded students.

notes.title: Pass/not-pass grade threshold and limits
notes.summary: P represents a grade of C- or better; N is below C-. The option may cover up to 20% of the 120-credit graduation requirement and at most two courses per academic year, defined as Fall–Summer. It cannot be elected for a course already completed with a letter grade. These limits are concurrent, not alternative permissions.

notes.title: Pass/not-pass language and study-abroad conditions
notes.summary: Elective study-abroad credit may use P/NP; when an institution reports only P/NP, Purdue applies its letter-grade calculation process. To receive lower-level language credit from placement, the Department of Languages and Cultures requires the advanced course to be taken for a letter grade. This page does not specify that calculation or placement-credit amounts.

notes.title: Historical Spring 2020 grading exception
notes.summary: Only for Spring 2020, all courses completed in Pass mode may meet any College of Science undergraduate degree requirement. This historical exception does not establish a current general waiver.

summer-math-exams.title: Purdue Math Summer Exam Policy and FAQ
summer-math-exams.locator: main#content, excluding breadcrumbs and navigation/sidebar; all policy text and visible link targets
summer-math-exams.heading: Purdue Math Summer Exam Policy and FAQ

notes.title: Math exam delivery from Summer 2026
notes.summary: The summer policy page states that starting Summer 2026 all Purdue Math courses, including online and distance courses, require all exams, including finals, in person on campus or at an approved testing center. Primary Online MA sections are explicitly covered. The title and planning guidance concern summer; the broader opening wording is retained without independently certifying its year-round scope. Students must plan travel or center access, fees and instructor exam windows.

notes.title: Math testing-center selection and cost
notes.summary: Students select and schedule their own approved center; instructors do not assign one. The Math Department offers on-campus exams without charge; Purdue Testing Services and other centers charge fees, with $35 per exam given as the Purdue Testing Services example. Students pay centers directly; charges cannot be billed to the Purdue account or reimbursed. NCTA-certified centers are recommended; international centers must communicate in English. Instructor syllabi/Brightspace supply dates and windows; early booking is advised.

notes.title: Math testing circumstances and accommodations
notes.summary: Students with DRC-approved accommodations coordinate with DRC and the testing center and notify the instructor in advance. If no approved center is nearby, they should contact the instructor or Math Department early. Students in multiple summer locations must secure a center for each exam. These directions do not promise an exam-mode exception. The page advises an in-person section or delayed enrollment if the stated arrangements cannot be met.

notes.title: External summer math and fall prerequisites
notes.summary: External math may be possible after equivalency-guide and advisor review. After completion, students must request an official transcript and contact the advisor to ensure the prerequisite is posted. The page strongly recommends Purdue for summer math needed as a fall prerequisite: transfer processing may take seven weeks and can prevent registration for the dependent fall course. No automatic transfer equivalence, credit award or prerequisite waiver is established.
